output.brief:
The fall in incidents is not real. Analysts still confirm about 36–37 incidents a month, the same as before. But 47 of them (23 in September, 24 in October) were moved out of the "confirmed" category by a script. The script runs from a Brackwater analyst host using the integration account. It polls every five minutes for cases with an SLA warning and changes their category 1–12 minutes later, shortly before the 4-hour containment deadline. Those cases then drop out of the containment and SLA figures. That is why containment looks like 100% and mean time to contain looks better. None of the 47 has a containment timestamp. I'm confident in this. What I can't tell is who at Brackwater wrote the script, or why. Nor can I tell whether the 28 deprecated detection rules let attacks through, because I didn't check that.

Do not cut the IR retainer or pay the 60k bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases and have your team and Halvard check containment on each. Remove category-write rights from the Brackwater integration role. Keep the logs. Ask Brackwater for a written explanation. Hold off on service-credit claims until that is settled. Then review the 28 dropped rules.
